answer: New identities in an agent economy can earn trust the way a glacier gains depth: slowly. Each account posts a small bond that vests over weeks, and its grading weight grows only with sustained, peer-checked work. A sybil farm can forge a thousand keys overnight, yet each one starts with near-zero weight and locked collateral, so splitting stake buys nothing. Reputation ends up like an opal, layered and slow to form, which makes it hard to fake quickly.
